A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cascading KV Cache research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original latency, PG19 perplexity, BookSum, LongBench, passkey retrieval and MMLU results, together with ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds InfiniteBench evaluations, additional baseline comparisons and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The core cascading-cache method is retained. Appendix C.1 adds a Cascade+MInference variant that replaces dense attention in the leading stride with MInference. Algorithm 2 also changes eager insertion from empty to non-full caches, aligning that condition with behavior already illustrated in v2 Figure 4.

E1.justification: v3 adds InfiniteBench en.MC, en.QA and en.Sum evaluations, extending English long-context multiple-choice, question-answering and summarization coverage (Table 10). PG19, LongBench, BookSum, MMLU and synthetic passkey retrieval remain; the new BookSum subsection discusses an existing evaluation.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens comparison with sparse-attention approaches: MInference and PyramidKV join the Llama 3.1 8B LongBench comparison, alongside Cascade+MInference (Table 9). MInference and the hybrid also enter latency comparisons (Tables 6 and 8). The Flash Attention 2 naming clarification does not establish a separate new comparator.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce a 32,768-token InfiniteBench cache, a 100K stride for Cascade+MInference, and all-layer latency measurements supplementing the existing single-layer study. Retained benchmark protocols remain substantially unchanged. Newly specified head pooling and existing Flash Attention prompt truncation are documentation additions.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a focused analysis of how combining cascading caching with MInference affects latency scaling, including the crossover beyond 131K tokens in Table 8. Existing stride, token-selection, cascade-count and head-policy ablations are retained; InfiniteBench scores alone are not counted as supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions omit error bars and retain 20 passkey trials per insertion-range/sequence-length combination, totaling 600 retrievals. v3 explicitly states the five ranges and six lengths already represented in v2. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals or statistical tests appear.

E6.justification: Substantial result sets are added while original benchmark scores are retained. Table 9 reports a 36.96 LongBench mean for the new 100K-stride hybrid; this is not a same-setting improvement of the original method. Table 10 reports InfiniteBench means of 35.32 for Cascade, 30.50 for Streaming LLM and 31.31 for truncated MInference. Tables 6 and 8 add latency and memory-limit findings.

T1.justification: v3 distinguishes overall sparsity, 1 - |C|/S, from cache-window sparsity, 1 - |C|/S_tilde; v2 defines only the latter as overall sparsity. Appendix C.2 adds a bound on the hybrid attention-block dimensions. The token-span derivation in Equation 4 remains, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same training-free context-extension, fixed-cache efficiency and performance claims, including the 12.13% LongBench improvement and 6.8-fold prefill speedup. The added appendix evidence does not redefine those central claims.

C2.justification: The new BookSum discussion explicitly acknowledges quadratic methods' quality advantage and latency cost. Appendix C.2 explains the hybrid's scaling through bounded attention chunks. Section 5 corrects the future-search objective from linear to subquadratic complexity, consistent with its retained O(N log N) proposal.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands implementation disclosure with Algorithm 3's Flash Attention 2 EMA-accumulation pseudocode, explicit CUDA/Triton kernel choices, independent-head/max-pooling settings and prompt-truncation details. It supplies a repository link in place of the supplementary-zip access statement. Hardware information is relocated, not newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to MInference, PyramidKV, InfiniteBench, Flash Attention 2 and ROUGE. Appendix C.1 positions Cascade against MInference's sparse prefill and PyramidKV's sparse decoding, and discusses integration with MInference. The main related-work narrative remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Changes include localized prose editing, a clearer positional-encoding explanation, a dedicated BookSum subsection, an experimental-settings appendix and additional comparison subsections. Publication headers and acknowledgments are added. The principal narrative and section sequence are substantially retained.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation expands substantially through new latency, sparsity-comparison and InfiniteBench tables, Algorithm 3 and Figure 18's prefill illustration. Former Table 6 becomes an expanded Table 9. Existing displays are also revised through cache-limit markers, an MMLU complexity column, the corrected Figure 12c subtraction label and figure relocation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves implementation transparency through Algorithm 3 and explicit settings, while additional comparators, InfiniteBench results and all-layer latency measurements strengthen empirical support. The gains are incremental: central results remain unchanged, and the new accuracy comparisons focus on Llama 3.1 8B with truncation or stride differences that limit broad comparative conclusions.
